summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expands the direct public-company universe around the hypothesized CRMN / defense surge-capacity qualification layer. The most relevant lane is not prime contractors but public digital-manufacturing platforms, additive-manufacturing equipment vendors, and on-demand factories with aerospace-defense certifications, secure workflows, supplier networks, or DoD program evidence. Current evidence supports a watchlist, not a thesis upgrade: CRMN authorization and possible RDT&E launch funding are policy signals, while company-level survivability depends on actual appropriations, awards, qualified lines, CMMC/ITAR/AS9100 scope, and recurring defense production conversion. Layer 1B expands the CRMN/surge-capacity qualification node into US-listed public equities tied to scarce qualification infrastructure rather than finished weapons demand. This remains a policy-to-appropriation hypothesis: candidates should stay in watchlist status until CRMN funding, program participation, direct contract awards, or disclosed defense revenue conversion is verified.
